ko.executive_summary: TSMC and Samsung are redirecting capacity toward advanced nodes, creating a supply vacuum in mature 8-inch fab capacity that Chinese foundries SMIC and Hua Hong are rapidly filling. This shift has immediate BOM implications for PMIC sourcing, as tier-1 suppliers face capacity constraints and geographic concentration risk.
key_facts: TSMC and Samsung shifting capacity away from mature nodes
SMIC and Hua Hong gaining share in 8-inch fab demand
Geographic supply concentration moving to Chinese foundries

implications.text: PMIC supply increasingly dependent on Chinese fabs (SMIC, Hua Hong); reduces supplier redundancy and introduces geopolitical risk for tier-1 buyers.
TSMC/Samsung exit from 8-inch creates tight mature-node capacity; Chinese fabs may leverage pricing power despite cost-leadership positioning.
Shift to SMIC/Hua Hong for volume PMIC production may extend qualification cycles for automotive and server-grade certifications.

ko.counterpoint: Chinese foundries have been investing aggressively in 8-inch capacity and mature process portfolios, suggesting they may absorb demand without major bottlenecks if execution remains on track.
